dependencies.reason: adds forge access, the label rules and the trailer fields to specrun's loop and ledger
the AF-Run trailer carries the counts of speca --gate-report

tasks.title: Reach the forge, create the label scheme, and give every open item a kind and its labels
steps: Add the behaviours as tests and confirm they fail; add to the helpers of internal/specrun an in-memory implementation of issuex.Client that holds issues, labels and comments, records every call in order and can fail a named call
Use github.com/agent-fox-dev/aflib/issuex for every forge operation; cmd/specrun still imports nothing that depends on agentkit-go, and the module's internal/issuex is not used

At start make the client for the repository of the origin remote with the token the issue command reads; when none can be made refuse at stage preflight, naming the token variables or the remote. Under --dry-run warn forge_unavailable instead, go on, and make no forge write in any case

Before the first step create every label of the scheme with CreateLabel, treating a conflict as a label that exists: the four kinds, the four severities, af:accepted, af:rejected, af:repair-failed, and af:from-<NN> and af:awaits-<NN> for each package under the spec root and its archive

In skills/af-impl/references/conformance.md say that every entry of the unmet list gets exactly one kind, with the four definitions of the PRD's section 1, and that a defect gets one of the four severities

In skills/af-impl/references/landing.md file each issue with its labels through `issue --create --label`: af:<kind>, af:from-<NN>, af:awaits-<NN> for awaits and af:severity-<s> for a defect; create a label that is missing with `issue --create-label` first; keep the body's 'What closes it', which for awaits names the receiving package by id
Document the scheme and the refusal without a forge in docs/specrun.md and the token variables in docs/configuration.md
done_when: `go list -deps ./cmd/specrun` names no package of agentkit-go

tasks.title: Check the labels of a landed package's issues
steps: Add the table of issues, the second application and the failing forge call as tests and confirm they fail

After the landing checks of a package pass, list its open issues: those labelled af:from-<NN> and those whose title starts with the package's directory name and a colon, following an incomplete listing to its end

For an issue that lacks a kind, lacks af:from-<NN>, is a defect without exactly one severity, is awaits without an af:awaits label, or carries two kinds: remove its other kind labels, add af:deviation and, when missing, af:from-<NN>, and add one comment naming the rule incomplete-labels, what was missing and the commit of the base branch

Make every label rule a function from the issues and the packages to a list of changes, applied afterwards, so that it is tested without a session and the dry run of a later package can print the list

A forge call that fails stops the loop after the package's ledger line is written, with the rule and the error in result.stopped; at the next start apply the rule for the last landed package again before choosing a step

tasks.title: Write the AF-Run trailer and read it into the ledger
steps: Add the trailer cases to the ledger tests and confirm they fail

After a landing read the trailers of the merge commit at the tip of the base branch with git, take the value of AF-Run, and decode it as one JSON object; copy its gate and open_items objects into the ledger line unchanged and ignore its other keys

Add the full gate runs and seconds, the reused gates and the number of items opened to the short form printed on stderr; with no trailer, or one that is not a JSON object, warn trailer_missing with the commit and write the line without the two objects

In skills/af-impl/references/landing.md end the merge commit message with the trailer `AF-Run: <one line of JSON>` after the Spec trailer's block: gate copied from `speca <package> --gate-report --since <baseline commit>` (full and task with runs, seconds and reused, baseline_full_seconds, last_full_seconds) and open_items with opened, closed, passed_on and reclassified, each an object of counts keyed by kind, a defect as defect:<severity>; closed, passed_on and reclassified are empty objects until af-impl reads items back
In the same file and in §8 of skills/af-impl/SKILL.md add the counts of open items per kind and severity, with the issue links, to the merge commit's open-items section and to the report
Document the trailer's keys and the ledger's new fields in docs/specrun.md
